note: Issue 4629 is a crash/ICE, so the predicate is internal_failure and NOT a text match on the reported 'llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type!'. Three independent reasons, all visible in the issue itself: (1) llvm-beanz's backtrace shows the assertions-enabled build stops at assert(false && "expected struct bitcast to only be used by lifetime intrinsics") in ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp RewriteBitCast -- that message contains no 'cast<X>' substring, so a contains/regex predicate on the reported text scores the Debug ground truth as clean; (2) the Windows build prints 'llvm::cast<X>()' where the Linux build behind Compiler Explorer prints plain 'cast<X>()', so a text marker is not portable across builds; (3) an internal failure may print nothing at all on older releases. is_internal_failure() keys on the specific statuses dxc's internal-error paths define (0x80000003, 0xE0000001-3, 0xC0000005, 0x80AA0018/1B/1D, POSIX signals) plus build-agnostic text markers, so it catches the trapped assert here, an access violation elsewhere, and the DXC_E_LLVM_CAST_ERROR path that the driver reports as plain E_FAIL. It deliberately does NOT fire on an ordinary diagnosed error: a syntax error, an unknown profile and a DXIL validation failure all exit 0x80004005 too. Control: control-nointerface.hlsl is the same shader with the interface inheritance removed; it must score no-match, proving the predicate is not simply firing on this file.
